title: Single-lead ECG arrhythmia classification on a microcontroller

record.title: Single-lead ECG arrhythmia classification on a microcontroller
record.abstract: Arrhythmia classification in wearable cardiac monitors demands algorithms compact enough to execute entirely on the sensor node, eliminating reliance on continuous cloud connectivity. This paper describes the design and validation of a single-lead ECG arrhythmia classifier implemented on a low-power 32-bit microcontroller (ARM Cortex-M0+, 48 MHz, 32 kB RAM). The classifier distinguishes five rhythm classes—normal sinus rhythm, atrial fibrillation, premature ventricular contractions, supraventricular tachycardia, and noise—using a lightweight feature set comprising RR-interval statistics, QRS morphology descriptors, and a three-stage decision-tree ensemble. Memory-efficient quantization reduces all floating-point parameters to 8-bit fixed-point representations without measurable accuracy loss. Evaluated on a held-out split of 4,200 annotated 30-second segments, the on-device model achieved a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.87 and consumed an average of 1.4 mW during inference, enabling operation for more than 72 hours on a 180 mAh coin cell. The work demonstrates a practical pathway toward fully autonomous, battery-powered cardiac monitors suitable for remote patient monitoring in resource-limited settings.
